chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Sayf, from his brother Al-Hussein, from his father Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was asked about the most knowledgeable of people. He replied: 'It is one who combines the knowledge of the people with his own knowledge.'

key_terms.جَمَعَ عِلْمَ النَّاسِ إِلَى عِلْمِهِ: Combined the knowledge of the people with his own knowledge

ai.seo_question: Who is considered the most knowledgeable person according to Imam Ali in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali (AS) defines the pinnacle of knowledge not merely as accumulation, but as the synthesis of universal human insight with the Imam's unique, divinely-anchored understanding (*'Ilm al-Ladunni*). This highlights the Shia doctrine of the Imams' comprehensive epistemology, where their knowledge acts as a unifying lens that contextualizes and perfects the fragmented knowledge of the broader community.
